concepts.title: Fractions: Sharing Equally
concepts.definition: When a whole number of things is shared equally, fractions tell how much each share is: a fraction names equal parts of a whole, written with a numerator above a denominator.
concepts.key_idea: A fraction is a share: the denominator counts the equal parts, the numerator counts the parts taken.

shade 3/5 of the given figure

solution_steps.explain: Say the rule in your own words.

Verify by reversing or re-counting, then conclude.

concepts.title: Equivalent Fractions
concepts.definition: Multiplying or dividing both numerator and denominator by the same number gives an equivalent fraction: 2/3, 4/6 and 6/9 are all the same share drawn with more parts.
concepts.formula: new_num = num * k; new_den = den * k
concepts.key_idea: Same share, more pieces: multiplying top and bottom by the same number changes the picture, not the value.
question_patterns: write two fractions equivalent to 2/3
how do you get an equivalent fraction of any fraction
is 4/6 equal to 2/3 justify
fill the blank to make equivalent fractions 3/5 = ?/20
why must we multiply both parts by the same number
reduce 6/9 to its simplest form

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the top by the chosen number.
Multiply the bottom by the same number so the share stays equal.

concepts.title: Adding Fractions with the Same Denominator
concepts.definition: Fractions with the same denominator add by adding their numerators while the denominator stays: 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7, since adding shares of the same size just counts more such shares.
concepts.key_idea: Equal pieces add piecewise: count the sevenths, and the denominator simply repeats.
concepts.textbook_ref: fegp107.txt, Addition and subtraction of fractions
question_patterns: add 2/7 and 3/7 and give the answer
how do we add fractions with the same denominator
subtract 1/9 from 5/9

add 3/11 and 4/11 and reduce if needed
solve a word problem using addition of like fractions

solution_steps.explain: Like fractions measure the same piece size, so the bottoms are equal.
Add the tops and keep the common denominator.

concepts.title: Mixed Numbers and Improper Fractions
concepts.definition: A mixed number pairs a whole with a fraction, like 2 1/3, while an improper fraction, like 7/3, keeps a numerator bigger than or equal to the denominator; the two forms describe the same amount and convert into each other.
concepts.key_idea: Whole and parts are interchangeable: 2 wholes and a third is the very same amount as 7 thirds.

solution_template.explain: Multiply the top of the fraction by the chosen number.
